# Cōātlīcue, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *coatlicue*. This is the file on how **Cōātlīcue** replaced it.

Cōātlīcue's best-known myth is the birth of the sun god Huitzilopōchtli, a story of cosmic matricide in which one child is chosen and the others are cast into the sky. The narrative is preserved in the Florentine Codex and colonial Nahuatl histories; it fuses divine genealogy with political theology. While Cōātlīcue was sweeping on the sacred mountain Coatepec, 'Serpent Mountain,' a ball of feathers descended and she placed it in her bosom.  By this she conceived Huitzilopōchtli.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Cōātlīcue
- **ASCII form:** coatlicue
- **Meaning:** "She of the serpent skirt"
- **Domain of influence:** Earth, Mother of Gods
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 58 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Cōātlīcue** to *coatlicue* and 3 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **o → ō** — Macron: long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.
- **a → ā** — Macron: long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.
- **i → ī** — Macron: long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Cōātlīcue** lives at [/sites/coatlicue/](/sites/coatlicue/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/coatlicue/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/coatlicue/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/coatlicue/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Cōātlīcue** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Wedding, Family & Maternity** — The mother of gods; the skirt of serpents that bore the sun.
- **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** — The earth mother who feeds and devours.
- **Environmental & Climate Services** — The living earth that sustains and reclaims.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
